content.title: Main versus cross
content.text:
For a row, the main axis runs left-to-right and the cross axis runs top-to-bottom.

For a column, the main axis runs top-to-bottom and the cross axis runs left-to-right.

The safe memory is not “justify means horizontal.”

The safe memory is:

**justify = main axis**

**align = cross axis**

options.text: Center the flex items along the row's main axis.
Center each letter inside every button.
Turn the row into a column.

feedback.correct: A row's main axis is horizontal, so `justify-content: center` centers the flex items across that available main-axis space.
feedback.incorrect: A row's main axis is horizontal, so `justify-content: center` centers the flex items across that available main-axis space.

feedback.correct: For a row, the cross axis is vertical. `align-items` controls how the flex items sit across that axis.
feedback.incorrect: For a row, the cross axis is vertical. `align-items` controls how the flex items sit across that axis.

activities.title: Tiny lab
activities.instruction: Complete the code challenge in the workspace, then run checks.

content.prompt:
Make a toolbar 300px wide and 80px tall. Put three buttons inside.

Experiment with:

```css
justify-content: center;
align-items: center;
```

Observe the two directions separately.

Then switch the flex direction to column and ask yourself what “main” and “cross” now mean.

feedback.incorrect: Check the requirements and compare your code with the expected structure.

content.title: Common trap
content.text:
People often memorize:

“justify = horizontal”

That memory fails when the direction changes.

The safer rule is:

**Find the main axis first. Then decide what `justify-content` is controlling.**

content.question: If you change a flex container from row to column, should your mental model of the axes stay tied to the words horizontal and vertical?

options.text: No. The axes are defined by the flex direction.
Yes. Main axis always means horizontal.
Yes. Cross axis always means vertical.

feedback.correct: The axis names describe the flex relationship, not permanent screen directions.
feedback.incorrect: The axis names describe the flex relationship, not permanent screen directions.

content.title: Forge takeaway & Lesson completion
takeaways: **Mental model:** Ask where the main axis points before choosing alignment properties.
**Senior habit:** Do not memorize the screen direction. Trace the container's chosen axis.
**Mastery signal:** You can predict what a justify or align change will do even after switching the flex direction.
